title: Coefficient actions under free-resolution computation of Tor
statement:
Let $R\to A\xrightarrow{g}B$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings, with $R\to B$ their composite, and let $M$ be an $R$-module. Let $P_\bullet\to M$ be a free resolution: its terms $P_j$ are free $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-free-module], $j\geq0$, and its augmented sequence $\cdots\to P_1\to P_0\to M\to0$ is exact. Put $P_j=0$ for $j<0$. For $S=A,B$ put $C(S)_\bullet=P_\bullet\otimes_R S$, without its augmentation, using [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. For every $n\geq0$, the canonical resolution-computation isomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]
$$\iota_{S,n}:\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,S)\longrightarrow H_n(C(S)_\bullet)$$
is $S$-linear for the coefficient action of [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module] (applied with coefficient ring $S$) and the action on homology induced by multiplication in $S$: explicitly, if $\iota_{S,n}(t)=[\sum_i p_i\otimes s_i]$, then
$$\iota_{S,n}(s\cdot t)=[\sum_i p_i\otimes ss_i]\quad(s\in S).$$
Moreover the $A$-action on $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$ specified by [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module] is the restriction of this $B$-action along $g$. In particular $(g(a)b)\cdot t=a\cdot(b\cdot t)$ for $a\in A$, $b\in B$ and $t\in\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$. No flatness is assumed.

proof.text: The given free resolution is a projective resolution: for each term $P_j$, choose a basis $(e_i)$ as in [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. Given a surjective $R$-linear map $q:U\to V$ and an $R$-linear map $h:P_j\to V$, choose $u_i\in U$ with $q(u_i)=h(e_i)$. The formula $\widetilde h(\sum_i r_i e_i)=\sum_i r_i u_i$ is well defined by uniqueness of the finite basis expansion, is $R$-linear, and satisfies $q\widetilde h=h$. This is precisely the projective lifting property; no finiteness of the basis or flatness of a coefficient ring is used.

source.place: Tag 00LY (algebra-section-tor), free-resolution construction; elementary basis lifting to verify the projective-resolution hypothesis.

proof.text: Fix $S=A$ or $B$. For $s\in S$, multiplication $\mu_s:S\to S$, $u\mapsto su$, is $R$-linear, since $S$ is commutative. By [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], it induces $m_{s,j}=1_{P_j}\otimes\mu_s$ with $m_{s,j}(p\otimes u)=p\otimes su$. The tensor relations give $m_{s+s',j}=m_{s,j}+m_{s',j}$, $m_{ss',j}=m_{s,j}m_{s',j}$ and $m_{1,j}=1$, where $s'$ denotes a second scalar. On every generator $p\otimes u$, both $d_j m_{s,j}$ and $m_{s,j-1}d_j$ give $d^P_j(p)\otimes su$; hence these maps commute on the whole tensor product. Thus $m_s$ is a chain endomorphism, and its degree-$n$ map on homology is $[z]\mapsto[m_{s,n}z]$ by [def-weil-pbc-module-chain-complex-homology]. It is well defined because cycles map to cycles and $m_{s,n}(d_{n+1}w)=d_{n+1}m_{s,n+1}w$. The displayed ring identities descend to homology and give exactly its coefficient $S$-module structure.

source.place: Tag 00M7 (algebra-section-functoriality-tor), item (1), multiplication on the coefficient factor; the tensor relations and homology quotient give the displayed checks.

proof.text: Apply clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-tor-map-via-resolution-lift] with $i=n$, $N=N'=S$ and $\psi=\mu_s$, using the projectivity checked in step 1. It gives $\iota_{S,n}\circ\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,\mu_s)=H_n(m_s)\circ\iota_{S,n}$. By [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module], applied to $R\to S\xrightarrow{1}S$, the Tor endomorphism on the left is precisely $t\mapsto s\cdot t$. Step 2 identifies the right-hand endomorphism on a cycle $z=\sum_i p_i\otimes u_i$ with $[z]\mapsto[\sum_i p_i\otimes su_i]$. This proves the claimed formula. The canonical comparison is already an $R$-module isomorphism by [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]; in particular it is additive. Together with the formula, this makes it $S$-linear. It holds separately for both $S=A$ and $S=B$ and for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tag 00LZ (algebra-lemma-tor-welldefined) and the coefficient functoriality paragraph immediately following it in Tag 00LY; apply to multiplication, as in Tag 00M7 item (1).

proof.text: For $a\in A$, [def-trf-tor-coefficient-module] defines the $A$-action on $\operatorname{Tor}^R_n(M,B)$ using the $R$-linear endomorphism $B\to B$, $u\mapsto g(a)u$. The same definition applied to $R\to B\xrightarrow{1}B$ defines the $B$-action of the element $g(a)$ using that identical endomorphism. Applying the same Tor functor to equal maps gives $a\cdot t=g(a)\cdot t$ for every $t$. This is equality with the restriction of the $B$-action, not a newly chosen action. Therefore, by the $B$-module associativity already computed in steps 2 and 3, $a\cdot(b\cdot t)=g(a)\cdot(b\cdot t)=(g(a)b)\cdot t$. All constructions use the original free $R$-resolution without requiring $P_\bullet\otimes_R S$ to remain exact, so no flatness hypothesis has entered.
